 Live .  28,455 viewing 28455 viewing Carrick sacked as Manchester United head coach
 Summary
 Manchester United sack head coach Michael Carrick 
 Man Utd release a statement saying the club came to an 'extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary' 
 The decision comes after owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe met with executives Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in Monaco
 'It is time for the owners to explain themselves' says the Manchester United Supporters' Trust 
 Former Tottenham and Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino is 'ready to accept an offer' to replace Carrick - United have 'opened talks' with him
 It follows their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, which leaves them sitting in the Premier League's relegation zone
 Carrick took interim charge in January and led club to a third-place finish before signing two-year deal in summer

 'How did they not let him ride it out?' published at 11:17 GMT 11:17 GMT 
 Rio Ferdinand 
Former Man Utd defender on YouTube 
 Personally I am disappointed that they have got rid of him. The results and performances have been really bad. But that is a huge contrast since last season, he did ever so well last year. 
 This was his first bump in the road and first moment where things have not gone to plan. How did they not let him ride it out?
 I think he could have been given more time to rectify things.

 'It is time for the owners to explain themselves' - MUST published at 11:12 GMT 11:12 GMT 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United Supporters' Trust have just released a statement. It says: "Michael Carrick’s departure marks another depressing moment for Manchester United. We thank him for his service and for restoring hope during the second half of last season. His standing among supporters remains undiminished.
 "The reason Manchester United fans have continued to support Michael Carrick in recent weeks is that they know that responsibility for United’s problems do not primarily rest with him or indeed his predecessors as manager.
 "They lie with the ownership.
 "The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club. When INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but.
 "It is time for the owners to explain themselves and show some accountability."

 'Forever legend' published at 11:05 GMT 11:05 GMT 
 We expect to hear a lot of reaction from current and former Manchester United players throughout the day.
 Rio Ferdinand, a former Manchester United team-mate of Michael Carrick, is one of the first to speak out. He said on X , external : "Forever Legend! 
Showed dignity & class as always ❤️"
 Image source, Getty Images

 'Carrick's staff knew the writing was on the wall' published at 11:00 GMT 11:00 GMT 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter on 5 Live 
 Football's a strange business at the best of times and clearly, if you are going to dismiss a manager you're going to have another manager in place to take over from him. 
 I think those negotiations have been happening this week. 
 There was also a big meeting of various Ineos executives in Monaco yesterday, that Manchester United's chief executive Omar Berrada was committed to attend to go there. 
 I think that has just led to this process being elongated even though my understanding is that Michael Carrick's staff knew the writing was on the wall on Monday and knew what was going to happen but people are under contract, they have to fulfill their roles until such time as they're told not to.

 How did we get here? published at 10:53 GMT 10:53 GMT 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United's last match was a thrilling 4-4 with Aston Villa in which the club twice came from two goals down.
 But that left the club in the relegation zone with just eight points from their 10 Premier League matches.
 This week United's chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox met with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco and discussed Carrick's future at the club.
 Carrick, who had been attending training this week, left United's training base Carrington this morning.
 As Simon Stone reported , the decision to sack Carrick should trigger the arrival of USA men's national team boss Mauricio Pochettino.

 Man Utd confirm Carrick's departure published at 10:41 GMT 10:41 GMT Breaking 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United have just released a statement, confirming the dismissal of Michael Carrick. 
 It reads: "Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025-26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.
 "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.
 "Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.
 "The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible."
 Image source, Getty Images

 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter on 5 Live 
 Michael
Carrick arrived at Carrington just before 8am, he’s now left the building. 
 We’re
still waiting for absolute, official confirmation but I’m being told from a
very reliable source that Michael Carrick has been told he’s no longer manager
of Manchester United and that will, I expect, trigger the arrival of Mauricio
Pochettino as his replacement or though we’re not entirely sure when.

 Carrick sacked as Man Utd head coach published at 10:21 GMT 10:21 GMT Breaking 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter 
 Sources have told BBC Sport that Manchester United have sacked head coach Michael Carrick with the club sitting in the Premier League's relegation zone.
 This is a developing story - with more information to follow.
